title: Clothes-rack product rail hover animation
prompt_text: Build a "clothes-rack" product rail for the product grid in this codebase. WHAT IT SHOULD FEEL LIKE - Products hang from hooks along a straight horizontal rail. At rest each product hangs SIDE-ON, showing its side photo (rest angle ~84-93deg, varied per product so the row looks real). Price tags hang from the hooks and always face the viewer. - Hover (or keyboard focus) on a product turns it to face the viewer (0 degrees) near-instantly: ~0.12s to 90%, settled by ~0.18s, no wobble. On leave it turns back to its resting angle. - The rail scrolls sideways to show more products: wheel, trackpad, touch, keyboard, prev/next buttons, mouse drag with a fling, and resting the cursor near either end (the rail runs that way). - The rail is a shallow arch, ends ~18px lower than the middle, and every hook rides it as the row scrolls. - When the rail moves, every product swings like a pendulum from the top of its hook: the hook moves first and the hem lags behind; while the rail keeps moving the hem trails at a slight lean; when the rail stops the hem swings through past vertical and settles in ~3-4s. BEFORE YOU WRITE CODE 1. Find the product grid / product card component and how product images are loaded. List the files you will change and wait for my OK. 2. Check the product images. Ideal: front, side and back shots, cut out on transparent backgrounds, on the same canvas size, with the neck on the same pixel in all three. [CHOOSE: front + side + back shots exist | front shots only (use the FRONT-ONLY FALLBACK below) | one white sample per style, tinted per colourway (use TINTING below)] 3. Do not change routing, analytics events, add-to-cart handlers, or any class name, id or data-* attribute that other code reads. STRUCTURE (adapt to the framework in use) - A scroll container (overflow-x: auto, no scroll-snap) holding a single row of product cards. The rail itself is a separate, non-scrolling bar behind the row, positioned where the hooks bend over it. - Each card stays a link to the product, with aria-label="<name>, <price>". Inside it: .hanger__swing (aria-hidden="true") swings; pivot = top of the hook hook image .hanger__spin turns; axis = through the neck .face--front front photo one plane... .face--back back photo ...rotateY(180deg) .face--side side photo crossed plane: rotateY(-90deg), photo mirrored with scaleX(-1) so the shirt's front leads .face--far side photo rotateY(90deg), not mirrored price tag after the spin, so it paints on top - CSS: - card: position: relative; fixed aspect-ratio. - .hanger__swing: position: absolute; inset: 0; transform-origin: 50% 2% (top of the hook); perspective: 640px; perspective-origin: 50% 25%. Keep it transform-style: flat. - .hanger__spin: position: absolute; inset: 0; transform-style: preserve-3d; transform-origin at the neck; transform: rotateY(var(--rest)), with --rest set per card. - faces: position: absolute, same box; backface-visibility: hidden. Front and back use opacity: var(--fw); both sides var(--sw). - side-on a product is ~40% of its card wide: overlap neighbouring cards by ~20% of their width each side; give the hovered / focused / tapped card a higher z-index. Make the card itself pointer-events: none and add a hit area the width of the hanging product (~40%), widened to the whole card while that card is turned, so overlapping cards don't steal hover and a sleeve doesn't drop it. - NEVER put filter, opacity < 1, overflow: hidden, clip-path or mask on .hanger__spin. They flatten the 3D context. Opacity, masks and drop shadows go on the faces. MOTION (plain JavaScript, one requestAnimationFrame loop, no library) - Each frame, dt = min(seconds since last frame, 0.1). Step both springs below in fixed 1/120s slices (ceil(dt * 120) substeps), so a stiff spring keeps real time on a 30fps phone and a 144Hz monitor alike. - Rail motion, read FIRST each frame (before writing any styles): speed = -(scroller.scrollLeft - lastLeft) / dt // hooks' px/s, right = + railV = 0.5 * railV + 0.5 * speed railAcc = 0.5 * railAcc + 0.5 * (railV - previous railV) / dt - Turn, per card (angle a in rad, speed w): target = (hovered and not dragging) or focus-visible or pinned ? 0 : rest w += (-900 * (a - target) - 54 * w) * dt; a += w * dt spin.style.transform = `rotateY(${a}rad)` - Crossfade, per card, from the same angle. The fades OVERLAP so at least one photo is always solid (a single 1-x fade goes see-through at 45deg): c = cos(a)^2 --fw = smoothstep(0.2, 0.5, c) --sw = 1 - smoothstep(0.5, 0.8, c) - Swing, per card (angle s in rad, speed v): v += (-30 * k * sin(s) - 2.6 * v + (0.0011 * railAcc + 0.0036 * railV) * cos(s)) * dt s = clamp(s + v * dt, -0.45, 0.45) swing.style.transform = `rotate(${s}rad)` k is per card, 0.8-1.2 (heavier products lower), so the row never swings in lockstep. Positive rotate is clockwise and carries the hem LEFT, which is what a rail moving right does, so both rail terms are added, not subtracted. - Mouse drag: on pointerdown (mouse only) remember x and scrollLeft; past 4px of movement, capture the pointer and set scrollLeft as it moves. Hovered cards do not turn while dragging. On release, keep scrolling at the last rail speed, multiplying it by exp(-4 * dt) each frame, and swallow the click that ends the drag. - Prev/next buttons: scroller.scrollBy({ left: ±60% of its width, behavior: "smooth" }). - Edge run: on pointermove (not touch), zone = min(140px, 18% of the rail's width); depth into the left/right zone d = 0..1; edgeTarget = ∓720 * d² px/s (0 outside the zones; 0 on pointerleave and while dragging). Each frame ease towards it: edgeV += (edgeTarget - edgeV) * (1 - exp(-6 * dt)) and move the rail by edgeV * dt, clamped to its ends. Keep the rail's position in a float and write it to scrollLeft (resync the float when scrollLeft moves by more than 1px for any other reason). While |edgeV| > 40, hovered cards do not turn. - Arch: draw the rail as an SVG quadratic across the visible rail, "M0 (y+sag) Q500 (y-sag) 1000 (y+sag)" with preserveAspectRatio="none" and sag = 18. Measure each card's centre (offsetLeft + width/2) once and on resize; each frame lower each card by sag * u², u = clamp((centre - scrollLeft) / railWidth * 2 - 1, -1.4, 1.4). Without JS or with reduced motion keep a straight rail and no offsets. - Start the loop on scroll, hover, focus, tap or drag; stop it when the rail is still and every card has settled (|a - target|, |w|, |s|, |v| all tiny), snapping a to target and s, v, w to 0. TINTING (if one white sample serves every colourway) - Each face: isolation: isolate; inside it a .face__tint layer (background: var(--cloth); mask: url(photo) center / contain no-repeat) and the white photo on top with mix-blend-mode: multiply. - Prepare the photo: cut out, white at true white, folds' contrast stretched a little so they survive the multiply. Solid colours only; textured or printed colourways need their own photos. FRONT-ONLY FALLBACK (if there is no side shot) - Rest at 55-65deg instead of ~90deg (a flat photo vanishes edge-on) and drop the side faces. Add 10 slices behind the front photo, spread across translateZ -11px to 11px, each a darker solid colour masked by the front photo, and a black overlay with opacity 0.35 * (1 - |cos(a)|) for shade. FALLBACKS AND ACCESSIBILITY - No JS: a CSS-only turn, scoped under a class (e.g. .rack--css) that the script removes when it takes over. Register --fw and --sw with @property (<number>, initial 0 and 1) so they transition: .hanger__spin { transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), --sw 80ms, --fw 80ms 60ms; } .hanger:hover .hanger__spin, .hanger:focus-visible .hanger__spin { transform: rotateY(0deg); --fw: 1; --sw: 0; transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1), --fw 80ms, --fw 80ms 60ms; } - prefers-reduced-motion: no springs and no swing; the turn is instant. - Touch: native scroll drives the swing. [CHOOSE: a tap turns the product and a second tap opens it | a tap simply opens the product] - Keyboard: a visible :focus-visible ring; focus turns the card to face front; never block Enter from opening the product. - Animate only transform, opacity and the custom properties. No layout reads in the loop other than scrollLeft, read before any writes. DONE WHEN - At rest the products hang side-on at slightly different angles, showing their side photos; hovering one turns it to face front crisply, settled within ~0.2s, no wobble, and never see-through mid-turn. - Flinging the rail, or resting the cursor near an end, makes the hems lag behind the hooks, then swing through when it stops, then settle; tags never turn; the hooks follow the arched rail. - With JS disabled you get the CSS turn and a scrollable rail; with reduced motion, an instant turn and no swing. - No console errors; analytics and add-to-cart behave exactly as before; Largest Contentful Paint is no worse. - Finish with a summary of the files you changed and the dials to tune: turn stiffness/damping (900, 54), swing pull/damping (30, 2.6), and how hard the rail pushes the hem (0.0011 acceleration, 0.0036 speed).

title: Moon impact cinematic in Python
prompt_text: Build a 20-second 1080x1350 30fps cinematic in Python (numpy + opencv + PIL), no 3D software, CPU only. Story: the moon falls toward Earth, a steel rocket launches on an intercept, hits it, and the moon is pushed back into orbit. End frame matches the first so it loops. 1. Get the free NASA-based earth (day, night lights, clouds, specular) and moon textures from the three.js repo on GitHub. 2. Write a ray-tracer for two spheres: per-pixel ray-sphere hits, equirect texture lookup, one sun light. Earth: day/night blend with city lights on the dark side, clouds, ocean glint, blue rim plus a thin atmosphere halo. Moon: soft lunar shading with a little earthshine. 3. Stars: 9k points + a faint milky-way band, motion streaks when the camera moves fast. Scale star density with the field of view. 4. Shots: wide approach (0-3s), tracking shot behind the moon (3-6s), telephoto from low orbit with the moon over Earth's limb (6-9s), rocket launch with a glowing plume (9-11s), nose-cam rush into the moon (11-12.4s), impact (12.4s), moon recedes (12.4-17.6s), back to the opening wide shot. 5. Impact: white flash, 3-frame color inversion, camera shake, glowing crater with fissures that cool down, a shockwave ring across the surface, 3,000+ debris particles with streaks that cool from white to orange to grey. 6. HUD in a mono font: lunar distance in km (starts at 384,400), closing speed, countdown, small "render · schematic" tag. 7. Post: bloom, filmic tonemap, vignette, light grain, chromatic aberration only on the impact. 8. Sound with numpy, no melody: rumble that rises toward impact, soft clicks on 8th notes that speed up, low thumps on every cut, rocket roar, a huge low boom, half a second of near-silence, then airy breathing noise that ramps back into the opening. Low-pass at 7 kHz, -14 LUFS, true peak under -1 dB. 9. Render stills at key moments first and fix framing before the full render. Encode H.264 + AAC, faststart.
